$schema_note: Maps every byte offset (0-63) of each report shape to a named field. Checked by bin/ci against fixtures/*.json for full coverage. Reassembly across multiple physical reports is NOT modeled here because discovery found there isn't any: opcodes 0x40/0x41/0x42 are independently complete report types, not fragments of one larger logical message (see PROTOCOL.md).

fields.name: length
fields.meaning: length of the info-package array that follows (magic+cmd+subfields+inner-crc)

fields.name: status
fields.meaning: 0x00 on outbound request, 0x55 on device ACK (getDongleAndKeyboardStatus opcode reused as an ack marker)

fields.name: payload_then_padding
fields.meaning: the info-package array (length bytes, command-specific, see commands below), then 0x00 padding to offset 63

fields.name: length
fields.meaning: length of the data payload that follows

fields.name: payload_then_padding
fields.meaning: the data payload (length bytes, command-specific, see commands below), then 0x00 padding

fields.name: length
fields.note: always 56 for this opcode in every capture; the site calls it with no explicit payload -- 56 is a baked-in constant, not derived from an actual 56-byte payload. Numeric meaning of 56 itself is unresolved (see unresolved[]).

fields.name: checksum8
fields.formula: (opcode + length + 0) & 0xFF  -- no real payload bytes contribute

fields.name: padding
fields.meaning: always all-zero in every observed capture

infoPackagePayload.note: [magic 0xA5 0x5A, cmd=9, 0x00, len=3, innerCrc16(0x09,0x00,0x03)] -- innerCrc16 uses a SEPARATE CRC-16/ARC function (poly 0xA001 reflected, init 0xFFFF), precomputed by the vendor's bundler since inputs never change. Do not confuse with the outer report checksum above.

[magic, cmd=11, 0x00, len=0, innerCrc16(0x0B,0x00,0x00)] -- no data-packet follows (unlike cmd9/cmd10, N=0). Resolved Milestone 2 (2026-08-11) via live HID capture; see fixtures/page-switch.json and fixtures/raw/cap-page-switch-hidlog.json.

cmd11_switchToHomepage.note: "Switch to the homepage" button. Sequence: infoPackage(0x40) -> finish(0x42), no data-packet, no repeat loop.

cmd13_switchToPicturePage.note: "Switch to the picture page" button. Same 2-report shape as cmd11.

cmd15_switchToGifPage.note: "Switch to the GIF page" button. Same 2-report shape as cmd11/cmd13. HARDWARE CAVEAT: on the real-hardware verification run, this command was sent and cleanly ACK'd (no error) but produced NO visible change on the TFT -- the test device has no GIF ever uploaded (only a factory-default static picture), so this is consistent with an 'empty GIF slot' no-op rather than a wrong command, but was NOT visually confirmed to actually switch pages the way cmd11/cmd13 were. A future test with an actual GIF uploaded to the device would give a real visual confirmation.

cmd14_clearPicture.note: "Clear the picture" button. Same info+finish shape as cmd11/13/15, but sent 16x in a row (32 reports total) -- matches the vendor source's literal for(a=0;a<16;a++) loop, and independently confirmed by counting the full raw HID log (not just trusting the source). Structurally UNRELATED to "Clear GIF" despite the vendor's internal function name for this loop implying otherwise -- see the cmd18/19 unresolved entry below and scripts/vendor-source-excerpt.js's corrective note.

transactionStructure.note: One 'Update device time' click = a for-loop of 3 iterations (confirmed in vendor source), each iteration sending: cmd9 infoPackage(0x40) -> cmd9 dataPacket(0x41) -> finish(0x42) -> cmd10 infoPackage(0x40) -> cmd10 dataPacket(0x41) -> finish(0x42). Every outbound report receives exactly 2 identical inputreport ACKs from the device (byte offset 6 flipped 0x00->0x55, otherwise byte-identical to the request) AS OBSERVED VIA WEBHID -- see rawEventCounts below for the counted evidence behind that. IMPORTANT: this is the WebHID-transport count; see linuxHidrawTransport below -- at the native hidraw layer only 1 real ACK arrives per write, not 2.

pageSwitch.shape: infoPackage(0x40) -> finish(0x42) -- 2 reports total, no data-packet, no repeat loop.

clearPicture.shape: The 2-report infoPackage(0x40) -> finish(0x42) pair, repeated 16 times (32 reports total) -- matches the vendor source's literal for(a=0;a<16;a++) loop. All 16 repeats are byte-identical (the command carries no per-iteration state), the same way set-time's 3 repeats are.
clearPicture.resolvedBy: Milestone 2, live HID capture + full raw-log event count, 2026-08-11.

rawEventCounts.source: cap3 session, full window.__hidLog for one click (54 raw HID events), counted directly (not sampled) before deduplication into fixtures/cap3.json's representative-per-type entries
rawEventCounts.arithmeticCheck: sum(outCounts) = 3+3+6+3+3 = 18; sum(inCounts) = 6+6+12+6+6 = 36; 18+36 = 54, matching the raw log's total event count exactly -- every out report received exactly 2 in ACKs (inCount = 2 * outCount for every report type).

linuxInterfaceIdentity.note: Obtained directly via Linux shell access on the capture machine (not from browser JS -- the earlier draft of this phase incorrectly deferred this as unreachable; it only required a local shell, which was available all along).

configChannel.hidrawNode: /dev/hidraw5 (this machine, 2026-08-10 -- node numbers are not stable across reboots/replugs; re-identify by usage page/usage + descriptor hash, not by number)
configChannel.decodedDescriptor: Usage Page 0xFF60, Usage 0x61, Collection(Application): Usage 0x62 Input(count=64,size=8,data/var/abs), Usage 0x63 Output(count=64,size=8,data/var/abs). No Report ID item present -- confirms this is an unnumbered-report interface, consistent with WebHID's reportId:0.
configChannel.aclConfirmed: getfacl shows `user:ivan:rw-` on /dev/hidraw5 -- the udev rule (VID 28E9) grants uaccess correctly on this interface, confirmed for all 4 of the device's hidraw nodes on this machine, not just some (an earlier plan-review round had flagged inconsistent ACL as a risk based on partial evidence; re-checked and it's uniform here).

linuxHidrawTransport.resolvedBy: Milestone 1 (native Rust set-time implementation), confirmed empirically against real hardware on 2026-08-10/11 -- see also the plan-review discussion where reviewers disagreed on the theoretical answer before this was tested.
linuxHidrawTransport.write: A native write() to /dev/hidraw5 requires a leading 0x00 'report number' byte prepended before the 64-byte report -- 65 bytes total on the wire. This is the documented Linux kernel hidraw behavior for unnumbered-report HID devices (the descriptor above has no Report ID item, yet the kernel still expects a synthetic ID byte on write). Writing exactly 64 bytes (no prefix) produces garbage responses from the device (observed: a status byte of 0x0f instead of the expected 0x00/0x55, on an otherwise-matching report) -- NOT silence, an actual malformed reply.
linuxHidrawTransport.read: read() returns exactly 64 bytes, WITHOUT the leading 0x00 -- asymmetric with write(). This matches the same documented kernel behavior (reads of unnumbered reports are not report-ID-prefixed).
linuxHidrawTransport.ackCount: IMPORTANT CORRECTION to Phase 0's WebHID-based finding: Phase 0's browser capture observed exactly 2 identical inputreport events per outbound report. At the native hidraw layer, only ONE real ACK arrives per write. The '2 ACKs' pattern was a WebHID/Chrome-side artifact (e.g. dispatched to two internal listeners), not a fact about the wire protocol. Native code should expect and require exactly 1 ACK per write, not 2.
linuxHidrawTransport.hardwareConfirmation: The full 18-report 'set time' sequence, sent with this write/read form, produced a byte-perfect ACK for every report and set the keyboard's TFT to the correct time and date -- independently reconfirmed the next morning (2026-08-11) when the keyboard's own clock had correctly ticked forward overnight to match real time, i.e. it's a genuinely running clock that was set correctly, not a static value that happened to look right once. Hour, minute, and date were all visually confirmed correct on the physical screen both times. Weekday was NOT visually confirmed -- the TFT screen has no weekday field at all (confirmed by checking), so there is nothing to look at. Weekday correctness instead rests on: the encoding logic being unit-tested against every day of the week (src/time.rs), and the device accepting the byte via a valid ACK without error -- weaker evidence than a visual check, and named as such rather than folded into the same 'confirmed' claim as hour/minute/date.

unresolved.item: finish (0x42) length byte numeric meaning (why 0x38/56, not e.g. 0x00)
unresolved.tried: confirmed as a stable constant across 3 live captures and the vendor source (`finishScreenControlDataPacket()` called with no arguments every time); the checksum formula using this constant is verified exactly. Only the semantic reason for the value 56 itself is unknown -- it does not block using this command.

unresolved.item: "Clear GIF" (cmd 18 and 19) -- what the extra trailing 2 bytes mean
unresolved.tried: Live HID capture, Milestone 2 (2026-08-11): clicking "Clear GIF" sends TWO different inner commands, cmd18 then cmd19, each once (4 reports total: info18+finish+info19+finish -- no repeat loop, unlike "Clear the picture"). Both info-package payloads are 9 bytes (2 longer than every other command decoded so far): cmd18 = [165,90,18,0,1,5,16,1,0], cmd19 = [165,90,19,0,2,196,1,1,0]. Bytes 0-6 fit the established magic/cmd/0/N/crcHi/crcLo pattern (ga([18,0,1])=[5,16], ga([19,0,2])=[196,1], both confirmed). What N means is NOT established -- in set-time N lines up with "a data-packet of N bytes follows," but no data-packet (0x41) is ever actually sent for cmd18 or cmd19, so calling N a "data-packet length" here would be an unverified claim. The 2 trailing bytes [1,0] are identical for both commands; meaning unknown (page/slot index? fixed marker? too few data points to tell). Deliberately NOT shipped as a CLI command in Milestone 2 -- shipping a command whose trailing bytes aren't understood, on the strength of "the checksum matches," is exactly the half-understood shipping this project avoids. A follow-up milestone can capture this a few more times (different GIF slot, different starting state) to triangulate the trailing bytes, the way set-time's minute/second fields were triangulated from multiple captures in Phase 0.

fixtureSchemaNote: Every report in fixtures/*.json carries these required keys: transaction_id, command_index, fragment_index, direction, hid_method, report_id, payload_hex. fragment_index is always 0 for every report in this phase's fixtures -- discovery found opcodes 0x40/0x41/0x42 are independently complete report types, not fragments requiring reassembly (see $schema_note above), so the field exists per the fixture schema but carries no ordering information here.
